topic_summary: Responsibilities, escalation flow, and skill expectations for each SOC tier.

flashcards.front: What is the primary responsibility of an L1 SOC Analyst?
flashcards.back: Monitor SIEM alerts, perform initial triage (close noise, escalate true positives), and document findings.

flashcards.front: Which SOC tier typically owns deep incident investigation and forensics?
flashcards.back: L2 — they take escalations from L1, perform host/network forensics, and coordinate containment.

flashcards.front: Name two non-shift activities an L3 SOC Analyst owns.
flashcards.back: Threat hunting and detection engineering (writing/tuning rules, building playbooks).

flashcards.front: Define "escalation" in the SOC tier model.
flashcards.back: Passing an alert or incident from a lower tier to a higher tier after triage confirms the lower tier cannot fully resolve it.

flashcards.front: Why is documentation important for an L1 analyst?
flashcards.back: It creates an audit trail, helps L2/L3 pick up context fast, and feeds detection-tuning feedback loops.

questions.stem: Which tier should typically close a known false-positive alert without escalation?

options.label: A
options.content: L1 — triage and close, log the rationale

options.label: B
options.content: L2 — only L2 may close alerts

options.label: C
options.content: L3 — they own all alert closure

options.label: D
options.content: No tier — alerts are closed automatically

questions.explanation: L1's core role is alert triage; closing a confirmed false positive with documentation is exactly the L1 workflow.

questions.stem: An L1 analyst sees beaconing traffic to an unknown external IP from a finance workstation. What is the correct next step?

options.label: A
options.content: Mark the alert as informational and close it

options.label: B
options.content: Triage briefly (enrich + verify), then escalate to L2 for deeper investigation

options.label: C
options.content: Block the IP at the firewall and move on

options.label: D
options.content: Wait for the user to report a problem first

questions.explanation: Beaconing to an unknown destination from a sensitive workstation is a credible incident indicator — L1 enriches and escalates rather than closing or unilaterally acting.

questions.stem: Which of the following are typical L3 responsibilities? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: L3 focuses on proactive work (hunting, detection, tooling). Routine triage is L1.

questions.stem: True or false: every SOC alert must be escalated to L2 before being closed.
questions.explanation: Confirmed false positives and routine informational alerts are closed at L1 — escalation is reserved for alerts L1 cannot conclusively resolve.
